SMTO-UI-0048 — UI assets are missing

GUID: 77954290-e883-41ee-a387-46e4417bd0a9
Slug: ui-assets-missing
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO's Directory page, the page SMTO shows first when you open its main address, can't be shown because one of its installed page files is missing. Your saved conversations and settings are not affected.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Stop SMTO. Reinstall the installed app, or replace the SMTO folder with a fresh, complete copy of the same version (re-download or re-extract it). Then run ./install.sh and start SMTO. The missing page file comes with SMTO itself, so a complete copy puts it back.
  2. If you updated SMTO recently, make sure the update finished. Don't start SMTO from a half-copied or partly deleted SMTO folder. An interrupted update or copy can leave SMTO without some of its page files.
  3. After SMTO starts, open its main address in your browser again. The Directory page is read from the installed files each time it is opened.

What success looks like

  • Opening SMTO's main address shows the Directory page instead of an error.

If it still fails

  • Copy the error message from the browser and send it to the person who installed SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's data folder; it holds your conversations, and the missing file isn't stored there.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The /directory landing route (where / redirects) returned an error because the installed static asset directory.html is missing from the Agent UI static directory.

What this means

  • The directory route cannot serve its required installed directory.html shell asset. This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.

Why this can happen

  • The directory route cannot serve its required installed directory.html shell asset.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect packaged asset presence and installed build consistency.

How to fix it

  • CoreRoutes.directory serves STATIC_DIR/directory.html (src/agent_runtime/api/static/agent_ui/) via _static_shell_response, which raises HTTP 500 "Directory assets are missing." when the file does not exist. Restore the file from the matching release or checkout (for example git checkout -- src/agent_runtime/api/static/agent_ui/directory.html, or reinstall the aor-runtime package), then restart the Server; install.sh alone does not restore deleted source files, and the state directory is not involved.
  • Restore the matching application installation and its packaged static assets.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The matching installed directory page is served successfully.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.
